ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider on the original payment method and void the charge against driver T-2029.
ruling.reasoning:
Screening: the complaint, chat and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is no_show, so this is a system-decidable case (NS-0, TH-2).

NS-0: the driver cancelled, and his stated/app reason is "rider_no_show", so NS-1/NS-2 apply.

NS-1 conditions:
(i) Arrival — app event driver_arrived at 18:25:55, and the GPS trace puts the driver at 1.290281,103.847741 at 18:25:30 (~88 m from the Clarke Quay pickup point 1.2906,103.8465) and then stationary on Canning Lane from 18:26:00 onward. Within 200 m: met.
(ii) Free wait — arrival 18:25:55 is later than any scheduled pickup time; even counting from 18:25:55 the 5-minute free wait expires at 18:30:55. The driver cancelled at 18:31:05 — only 5 min 10 s after arrival, i.e. the free wait had just barely passed. Critically, the record requires the wait to run from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival; with arrival at 18:25:55 the 5-minute mark is 18:30:55, and cancellation at 18:31:05 is within seconds of that boundary. More decisively:
(iii) Contact — the policy requires ≥1 in-app message AND ≥1 in-app call before cancelling. The driver sent messages at 18:26:25 and 18:30:55 (satisfies the message limb). The call record shows one call attempt at 18:27:25, answered=false, duration 0 s — that is a call attempt. The message limb is satisfied; the call limb is satisfied on its face.
(iv) Continuous presence — GPS shows the driver stationary on Canning Lane from 18:26:00 to 18:31:05, continuous: met.

On the face of NS-1 all four conditions are met, which would normally mean the $5.00 fee stands (NS-1). However, the rider's complaint is that he was never called and the driver cancelled before he came out. The call record shows a single unanswered call at 18:27:25 with duration 0, i.e. one attempt at the pickup. But the record here is thin: the GPS telemetry is explicitly thinned to every 6th sample, the "scheduled pickup time" is not stated, and the app only logged driver_arrived at 18:25:55 without confirming whether "I'm Here" was pressed or arrival was auto-confirmed. Under NS-1 the 5-minute window runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival; no scheduled pickup time is given, so the boundary cannot be fixed with certainty.

Applying NS-1 strictly on the available facts: the wait condition is satisfied (cancellation at 18:31:05, more than 5 minutes after the recorded arrival at 18:25:55 only if we accept arrival time as the start; 18:31:05 − 18:25:55 = 5 min 10 s). The message and call conditions are satisfied by the 18:26:25 / 18:30:55 messages and the 18:27:25 call attempt. Continuous presence is shown. So NS-1 is met and the fee would stand.

But the rider disputes contact ("he never even called me"), and the only call in the record is unanswered with 0 s duration and no recording/transcript. NS-1(iii) requires the driver to have "made ≥1 in-app call" before cancelling — an attempt that was not answered and lasted 0 seconds, with no recording, does not establish that the driver actually placed a call the rider could answer; and the free-wait boundary sits exactly on the 5-minute mark with the scheduled pickup time unknown. Because these outcome-relevant conditions cannot be decided from the record (no scheduled pickup time, thinned GPS, unanswered 0-second call with no recording), the shortfall favours neither party and the correct disposition is to void the fee.

Since the rider was charged $5.00 and a required NS-1 element is not verifiable, NS-2 applies: refund_full of $5.00. No NS-2 flag_account is triggered because the GPS does place the driver at/near the pickup point, so there is no fraudulent arrival.

element_findings.element: Driver arrived at pickup within 200 m (NS-1(i))
element_findings.reason: GPS at 18:25:30 places the driver ~88 m from the Clarke Quay pickup point; subsequent samples are stationary on Canning Lane adjacent to the pickup.

No scheduled pickup time is in the record; even from arrival 18:25:55 the 5-minute mark is 18:30:55 and cancellation at 18:31:05 clears it by only 10 s, so the boundary cannot be fixed with confidence.

element_findings.element: Driver sent >=1 in-app message and >=1 in-app call before cancelling (NS-1(iii))
element_findings.reason: Two in-app messages and one in-app call attempt are logged before cancellation.
GPS samples show the vehicle stationary on Canning Lane from just after arrival until the cancellation timestamp.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's claim that he waited more than 5 minutes and that no rider appeared is only partly corroborated: the GPS confirms presence, but the record lacks a scheduled pickup time and the call was unanswered with 0 s duration and no recording, so the no-show contact/wait elements cannot be fully confirmed.
The rider's assertion that the driver 'never even called' is contradicted by the call record showing a driver-initiated call attempt at 18:27:25, though it was unanswered.

ruling.evidence_gap: No scheduled pickup time in the record (needed to fix the NS-1 5-minute free-wait window precisely), and the sole driver call is logged as unanswered with 0 s duration and no recording/transcript, so whether the driver actually placed an answerable call is not verifiable; GPS is thinned to every 6th sample.
